entry_conditions: This policy can start from the demonstrated home/open-gripper state or from an already-started approach to the red block when drawer_position is near closed, typically below about 0.02 m. It can also take over during the shared transition if causal observations show the red block and TCP are already near the drawer front/opened-drawer area and the phase cues are consistent with closing, pulling, release, or retreat. Required causal cues are qpos finger gap, qvel, tcp_pose, red_pose, drawer_position, and drawer_velocity in the world frame/metres.
exit_conditions: Hand off after the release/retreat state is visible: drawer_position is open, preferably greater than 0.26 m; finger width is near the demonstrated open value around 0.08 m total; red is no longer co-moving with the closed gripper; and the TCP is moving upward/away from the red block toward the demonstrated retreat posture. At the measured end of this slice the drawer is about 0.30 m open, the fingers are open, and the TCP height is roughly 0.37 m.
overlap_role: Indices 240:330 are shared with the successor red_top_regrasp_lift. This policy learns the end of the side-pull release and upward retreat, while the successor can use the same observations to begin preparing a top grasp once the drawer is open and the gripper is no longer clamped on the red block.
successor_readiness: The successor should receive an open-drawer/open-gripper observation rather than a closed-finger pull observation: drawer_position above the open threshold, gripper command/finger qpos indicating open fingers, red left on the open drawer surface, and TCP separated enough or rising enough that a top regrasp trajectory is plausible. A geometric drawer-open condition alone is not sufficient if the fingers are still closed on the red block.
failure_signatures: Potential failures include phase order skipping the close phase before pulling, fingers remaining open while drawer_velocity stays near zero during attempted pull, red_pose failing to move with the TCP during a supposed closed pull, drawer_position not increasing during the pull phase, or the policy continuing closed-finger pulling after drawer_position has saturated near 0.30 m. These are inferred from observations and are not measured force/contact guarantees.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy while drawer_position is below the open threshold, while fingers are closing/closed with red and TCP co-moving, or while the gripper is releasing immediately after the drawer reaches the open range. Transfer during the overlap when the causal history shows open fingers and retreat/open phase cues. If the policy is invoked partway through the overlap, it uses finger width, drawer_position, drawer_velocity, TCP-red displacement, and two-frame motion to infer whether to finish releasing or to keep retreating.
limitations: The handoff cues are based on demonstrated state observations, not force sensing or hard contact classification. The implemented model is a learned diffusion policy with a stateless soft phase belief from two observations; it does not maintain an external automaton state and cannot guarantee recovery from a missed grasp, block slip, or large off-distribution drawer pose.
